prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every Dallas roof replacement — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, roof type, budget, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, desired materials, and how important things like long warranties or manufacturer certification are to you.

I can help you find the best contractor for your situation. Before that, here are practical steps and questions to quickly identify a top-quality roofer in Dallas.

What to ask and check
- Are you licensed and insured? Ask for proof of liability insurance and workers’ compensation. Get the company’s insurance carrier name and policy number to verify.  
- Do you pull permits? A reputable Dallas roofer will obtain required city/county permits and inspections.  
- References and recent jobs: Ask for 3 local references and photos of recent similar jobs. Drive by if possible.  
- Manufacturer certifications: Look for GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, etc. These mean the crew is trained and you may get enhanced warranties.  
- Written estimate & contract: Must list materials, brand and model of shingles, underlayment, ventilation, removal of old roofing, disposal, start/completion dates, cleanup, and payment schedule.  
- Warranties: Material (manufacturer) and workmanship (contractor). Get both in writing and know who services the warranty.  
- Payment terms: Avoid paying full upfront. Typical deposit is 10–30% with balance due at or after completion and inspection. Never pay cash for entire job.  
- Insurance-claim experience: If filing a claim, ensure the roofer knows the claim process and will coordinate with adjuster, but beware of storm chasers.

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure sales and “today-only” deals.  
- No local address or ties to the Dallas area.  
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide certificate.  
- Demands for full payment upfront or insists on cash-only.  
- Extremely low bids far below other estimates (often cut corners or use inferior materials).

Where to look for reputable roofers
- Google Reviews and Yelp (look at patterns, not single reviews).  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) complaints & rating.  
- Angi/HomeAdvisor checks and customer reviews.  
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed certified contractor locators).  
- Local neighborhood Facebook groups or Nextdoor for personal recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short vetted list of top-rated roofers near your ZIP code (I’ll check reviews, certifications, BBB), or  
- Recommend what to look for for your specific roof type (asphalt shingle, tile, metal) and whether you’re using insurance.

Tell me your ZIP code, whether it’s residential or commercial, roof material, and if you’re filing an insurance claim — I’ll find a few well-reviewed options and summarize their strengths.
